references.text: Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him, fell on his neck and wept – almost identical wording to Joseph's reunion with his father.
Joseph fell on his brother Benjamin's neck and wept, and he kissed all his brothers and wept over them – a parallel emotional reunion scene.
Joseph was given Pharaoh's second-best chariot, and here he harnesses his own chariot to meet his father.
Joseph threw himself upon his father's face, wept over him and kissed him – a parallel emotional scene at Jacob's death.
The Lord told Aaron to go and meet Moses in the wilderness, and Aaron met him at God's mountain and kissed him – a reunion between family members after a long separation.
Both verses reveal Joseph's deep compassion and emotional vulnerability toward his family, regardless of whether it is a brother or father being reunited.
Both verses show Joseph's tears as a response to family circumstances: joy at reuniting with his father and empathy/grief when his brothers ask for forgiveness.
The parallel lies in the recognition of the 'father' role (biological or spiritual) and the expression of deep grief/love through weeping.
